about.text: Cheese eaten young, with little or no ripening, so it stays soft, moist and mild and keeps only briefly: under German cheese law it holds more than 73 % water in the cheese without its fat. Set with rennet, as these are, or mainly with acid, as quark and cottage cheese are.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

picks.why: Mexico's most common fresh cheese, a staple of everyday cooking across the country and the US.
The everyday fresh white cheese of Latin America, made and eaten across Mexico, Peru and Central America.
France's classic unripened curd cheese, eaten fresh at table and the base of countless dairy desserts.
Spain's best-known fresh cheese, a soft sheep or cow curd from Burgos eaten with honey or walnuts.
The Gulf region's staple white fresh cheese, widely eaten at breakfast across Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE and Qatar.
